summary: The implementation adds startswith/endswith to Query and passes the new tests, but there is a real defect: the query hash only includes ('startswith', self._path) — not the prefix/suffix value. This means where('name').startswith('Al') == where('name').startswith('al') is True, so TinyDB's query caching collides and returns wrong results when different prefixes are used on the same database. I verified this directly: on one DB, startswith('al') incorrectly returned ['Alice', 'Alan'] because it reused the cached result from startswith('Al').

checks.claim: startswith/endswith match strings correctly and skip non-strings/missing fields
checks.evidence: python -m pytest tests/test_startswith_seed.py -v → 6 passed (parametrized over MemoryStorage and JSONStorage)

checks.claim: hash collision between different prefixes causes wrong cached results
checks.evidence: python -c: where('name').startswith('Al') == where('name').startswith('al') → True; on same DB, startswith('al') returned ['Alice','Alan'] instead of ['alice']

findings.text: startswith hashval ('startswith', self._path) omits the prefix value, causing cache collisions between different prefixes. Same issue for endswith at line 259.
